title: Woody 'Blankets' Deployed on Arctic Permafrost to Cut Emissions
title_zh: 给北极冻土盖“木头毯子”，能减少碳排放吗？

image.credit: U.S. Department of Energy · cc0 1.0 · via rawpixel

paragraphs: A Canadian start-up is developing a way to curb greenhouse-gas emissions from permafrost by stabilizing the soil with an insulating 'blanket' of woody materials. Should the method prove effective, it would constitute the first tool designed specifically to forestall emissions escaping from permafrost as the Arctic warms. 'Our goal is to make sure the carbon in the soil remains buried,' says Cansu Culha, co-founder of PermaC and a natural-hazards researcher at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver.

Earth's frozen environments are thawing as temperatures rise in response to human emissions, and the only reliable global-scale remedy is to slash fossil-fuel emissions. Nevertheless, some researchers are exploring direct interventions, from reflective mats on glaciers to pumping water onto sea ice to thicken it. PermaC's approach, researchers say, is the first they know of to target permafrost thaw and its associated emissions, which are estimated to be equivalent to those of Japan.

The company has just completed the first test of its blankets in Canada's Northwest Territories, at a rapidly eroding feature known as a retrogressive thaw slump. Such slumps occur when a hill of permafrost thaws and collapses, allowing erosion to take big bites out of the landscape and exposing deeper soil to warming, thereby forming hotspots of CO2 and methane. One estimate suggests that rapid erosion could amplify permafrost emissions by as much as 40% compared with models accounting only for gradual thaw.

The approach stabilizes the slump's edge with a layer of wood shavings, soil and native seeds, plus a burlap-like mat of coconut husks. Culha says she got the idea after hearing about Indigenous communities in Alaska that prevent permafrost degradation by planting trees along slump edges. Similar erosion-control blankets are used in temperate areas, but until now they have not been deployed to insulate or stabilize permafrost, she says.

PermaC has yet to release results from this year's test, but the blanket appears to have halted erosion: over the Arctic summer, the unblanketed edge of the slump retreated by 5 metres, whereas the blanketed area saw no measurable retreat, Culha says. 'That's very promising,' says Christina Schaedel, a permafrost scientist at the Woodwell Climate Research Center in Falmouth, Massachusetts, who has been advising the company. However, she adds, the result comes from only one slump over one summer.

One challenge is calculating how much CO2 the blankets prevent from being emitted. Measuring emissions from slumps is not straightforward and remains an active research question, says Mark Lara, a biologist at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. 'There definitely are slumps that are spewing out carbon,' he says, but there are 'lots of minutiae that could dramatically impact the results'. So far, Culha has only rough estimates; she thinks about 2,200 tonnes of CO2 a year might be prevented at the average carbon-rich slump, and that installing blankets at 20,000 slumps across Canada and Alaska could prevent roughly 40 million tonnes annually, equivalent to Hungary's emissions.
paragraphs_zh: 一家加拿大初创公司正在开发一种方法，用木质材料制成的保温“毯子”来稳定土壤，从而减少冻土产生的温室气体排放。如果这种方法被证明有效，它将成为首个专门用来阻止北极变暖导致冻土排放气体的工具。“我们的目标是确保土壤中的碳继续埋在地下，”PermaC 联合创始人、温哥华不列颠哥伦比亚大学自然灾害研究员詹苏·库尔哈说。
随着人类排放导致气温上升，地球的冰冻环境正在融化，而唯一可靠的全球性解决办法是大幅削减化石燃料排放。尽管如此，一些研究人员仍在探索直接干预手段，比如在冰川上铺设反光垫，或把水抽到海冰上使其增厚。研究人员说，PermaC 的做法是他们所知第一个针对冻土融化及其相关排放的方案，而这些排放量估计相当于日本的排放量。
该公司刚刚在加拿大西北地区完成了首次毯子测试，地点是一处被称为“后退式热融滑塌”的快速侵蚀地貌。这种滑塌发生在冻土山丘融化坍塌时，侵蚀会大口吞噬地表，使更深的土层暴露在升温环境中，形成二氧化碳和甲烷的排放热点。有估算认为，与只考虑渐进融化的模型相比，快速侵蚀可能使冻土排放量增加多达40%。
这种方法用一层木屑、土壤和本地草种，再加上一张类似麻布的椰壳纤维垫，来稳定滑塌边缘。库尔哈说，她是在听说阿拉斯加原住民社区通过在滑塌边缘种树来防止冻土退化后产生这个想法的。她说，类似的防侵蚀毯在温带地区也有使用，但直到现在才被用来为冻土保温或稳定冻土。
PermaC 尚未公布今年测试的结果，但毯子似乎已经阻止了侵蚀：库尔哈说，在北极夏季，没有铺毯子的滑塌边缘后退了5米，而铺毯区域没有可测量的后退。“这非常有前景，”一直在为公司提供咨询的马萨诸塞州法尔茅斯伍德韦尔气候研究中心的冻土科学家克里斯蒂娜·舍德尔说。但她补充说，这一结果只来自一个滑塌点、一个夏季。

一个难题是计算毯子到底防止了多少二氧化碳排放。伊利诺伊大学厄巴纳-香槟分校研究冻土地貌的生物学家马克·拉拉说，测量滑塌点的排放并不简单，仍是一个活跃的研究问题。“确实有滑塌点在大量排放碳，”他说，但“有很多细枝末节可能极大地影响结果”。库尔哈目前只有粗略估计；她认为，在一个碳含量丰富的普通滑塌点，每年可能防止约2200吨二氧化碳排放，如果在加拿大和阿拉斯加的2万个滑塌点铺设毯子，每年可能防止约4000万吨排放，相当于匈牙利的排放量。

vocab.note: 北极气候报道中的高频词，指常年冻结的土壤。
比 prevent 更正式，常与 emissions、crisis 等搭配。
既可作动词也可作名词，是冻土话题的核心词。
专业地貌术语，指冻土融化坍塌后不断后退的侵蚀地貌。
来自动词 insulate，本义为隔热、绝缘。
常用复数 emissions，指温室气体排放。
一种强效温室气体，冻土融化时会释放。
新闻中常指稳定土壤、局势或价格。
科研语境中指根据现有数据推算更大范围的结果。
企业或个人购买以抵消自身排放的凭证。
正式用词，常指容易被忽略却影响结果的细节。

A Canadian start-up firm is developing a way to prevent greenhouse-gas emissions from permafrost by stabilizing the soil with an insulating ‘blanket’ of woody materials. If the method works, it could be the first tool to directly forestall green-house gas emissions that are escaping from permafrost as the Arctic heats.
“Our goal is to make sure the carbon in the soil remains buried,” says Cansu Culha, co-founder of PermaC and a natural-hazards researcher at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver, Canada.
Earth’s
frozen environments are thawing
as temperatures rise in response to human emissions. The only reliable way to slow that melting on a global scale is to slash emissions from the burning of fossil fuels. But some researchers are exploring methods to prevent the thaw directly, ranging from placing reflective mats on glaciers to pumping water onto sea ice to thicken it.

associated emissions

Culha says she got the idea after hearing about Indigenous communities in Alaska that prevent permafrost degradation by planting trees along the edges of slumps. 2
or methane after erosion.
